JUDGMENT :
[PER : SHYAM C. CHANDAK, J.] :-
1) Present Appeal filed under Section 11 of The Maharashtra P.H. Jayani 72 APEAL489.2023 FINAL.doc Protection of Interest of Depositors (In Financial Establishments) Act, 1999 (for short 'MPID Act') is seeking an exception to the Order dated 16 th February 2023, passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Pune whereby the learned Judge rejected the Criminal Miscellaneous Application No.229 of 2022 (for short 'the Application') filed under Section 156(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure seeking for direction to Shivaji Nagar Police Station, Pune to register F.I.R. and commence investigation for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 409, 420 read with Sections 120-B and 34 of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 3 and 4 of the MPID Act, against the Respondent Nos.2 to 6, who were arraigned as accused Nos.1 to 5 in the said Application.

sentences.text:
1.1) Hereinafter, the parties are being referred to by their original status in the Application i.e.,
Appellant and Respondent Nos.7 and 8 as 'Complainant Nos.3, 1 and 2 respectively' and Respondent Nos.2 to 6 as 'Accused'.
2) Heard Mr. Nashikkar, Advocate for the Appellant, Mrs. Takalkar, learned APP for Respondent No.1-State and Mr. Rajiv Chavan, learned Senior Advocate for Respondent No.2 to 6.
Perused the record.

3) The Complainants had filed the said Criminal M.A. No.229 of 2022 wherein it was narrated that,
the Complainant Nos.1 and 2 are housewives.
They wanted to invest their savings in a scheme giving descent returns.
The Complainant No.3 has been doing a business of metals in the P.H. Jayani 72 APEAL489.2023 FINAL.doc name and styled as 'Indus Metals'.
Accused no.1-M/s. Bhimashankar Developers is doing a business of development of real estate, construction and allied activities.
Accused Nos.2 to 5 are partners of accused no.1. 3.1)

In January 2018, the accused persons told the Complainant Nos.1 and 2 that, they have floated a real estate scheme i.e., 'Buy Back Scheme' in respect of Gat Nos.360 and 361, Amberwadi, Khandala, Satara wherein the money invested will give lucrative returns.

In the alternative, the Complainants will have an option to retain a plot No.27,
allotted as security/mortgage in the said land, instead of taking back the deposited money, upon payment of certain amount.
Relying upon said representations made by the accused, the Complainants agreed to deposit their money in the said scheme.

3.2) Thereafter, Complainant Nos.1 and 2 deposited Rs.1,00,000/- each with the accused persons on the promise by the accused that, they would return the said deposit along with a return totaling to Rs.17,20,291/- upon expiry of 2 years, in a phased manner in the form of postdated cheques.

Alternatively, the accused persons informed that, the Complainant Nos.1 and 2 will have an option of retaining plot No.27, upon payment of Rs.2,04,100/- at the time of handing over possession of the said plot.

Accordingly, the Complainant Nos.1 and 2 entered into a MoU dated 25 th January,
2018 containing the above details and the terms and conditions thereof.

sentences.text: At the time of MoU, the accused persons drew 12 post dated cheques for Rs.71,679/- each in favour of Complainant No.1 and 12 post dated cheques for Rs.71,679/- each in favour of Complainant No.2.
Upon expiry of the two years period, the Complainant Nos.1 and 2 requested the accused to pay the agreed returns.
However, the accused stated that, they are not in a position to pay the agreed compensation.
Thereafter, the Complainant Nos.1 and 2 deposited one post dated cheque each, however, said cheques dishonoured.

Therefore,
on 17 th March, 2022 the Complainant Nos.1 and 2 issued a legal notice to the accused to comply with the MoU but in vain.

3.4) That, in the similar manner, the accused persons caused the Appellant/Complainant No.3 to invest Rs.4,39,000/- in the same 'Buy Back Scheme' in respect of Gat No.369, Amberwadi,
Khandala, Satara, stating that, the invested money will give lucrative returns totalling to Rs.33,73,457/-.

In the alternative, the Complainants will have an option to retain plot Nos.79 and 80, allotted as security/mortgage, in the said land, instead of taking back the deposited money with the returns, but upon payment of Rs.3,47,300/- as balance consideration at the time of handing over possession of the said plots.
Accordingly, the Complainant No.3 deposited Rs.4,39,000/- and thereafter, entered into a MoU dated 24th July, 2017 containing the details as above and the terms and conditions thereof.
At the time of MoU, the accused persons drew total 12 post dated cheques P.H. Jayani 72 APEAL489.2023 FINAL.doc for Rs.2,81,121/- each in favour of Complainant No.3.
3.5) It is stated that, upon expiration of the stipulated two years period, the Appellant requested the accused to pay the agreed return of Rs.33,73,457/-.
However, the accused stated that, they are not in a position to pay the said amount due to financial crisis.
Thereafter, the Appellant followed up with the accused on numerous occasions but in vain.

Therefore, by letter dated 05th August 2019, the Appellant informed the accused that, they are liable to pay the compensation of Rs.33,73,457/-,
therefore he would deposit 1st of the said cheques.
Thereafter, all the PDCs dishonoured when presented for encashment.
The Appellant followed up with the accused and issued a notice dated 15 th March 2022 thereby demanding the said amount but it did not fructify.
It is stated that, the amount invested by the Appellant was siphoned to other shell entities and sister companies.

4) Thus, the accused persons deceived the Appellant and his co- Complainants and dishonestly induced them to deposit their money by floating nonviable development scheme in respect of the said land but without any intention to return the said deposited money along with the promised compensation/interest.

Therefore, the Complainants lodged their written complaint by post with the Shivaji Nagar Police Station, Pune and Deputy Commissioner of Police, EOW and Cyber Cell Pune,
on 03 rd May, 2022.
However, the police did not take any action on the said complaint.

sentences.text: After considering the Application and the submissions made by learned Advocate for the Complainants, the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Pune noted that, at the time of dishonour of the cheques itself the Complainants knew that, the accused persons were not in a position to repay the invested amount.
Thereafter, the Complainants persuaded with the accused persons for refund of their money.
From these facts, it is clear that, when the cheques were dishonoured, the Complainants got to know that, the transaction in question was of civil nature.
Therefore, the Complainants have not approached the police nor taken any step against the accused.
Hence, the Complainants failed to make out the case of the alleged offences to direct the registration of the FIR and investigation.
This led the learned Judge to reject the Application.
Hence, the present Appeal.
6) Mr. Nashikkar, Advocate for the Appellant submitted that, the accused persons had floated a completely nonviable scheme of the investment and returns.
This conduct itself manifests that, since inception there was intention on the part of the accused to cheat the Complainants.
After accepting the said investment, the accused persons siphoned that amount to shell entities/sister companies.
Thus, this is a clear case of cheating and misappropriation.

Considering the entire facts and circumstances of the case together, it is evident that, the amount invested by the Complainants is a 'Deposit' and the accused persons are falling in the P.H. Jayani 72 APEAL489.2023 FINAL.doc definition of 'Financial Establishments' as defined under Section 2 (d) of the MPID Act.

However,
the learned Judge completely ignored above and erroneously held that, the transaction in question is of civil nature.
Therefore, the impugned Order is not sustainable in law and is liable to be quashed.
To buttress his submissions, the learned Advocate placed his reliance on following decisions.
We have carefully considered the same.

i) State of Maharashtra vs. 63 Moons Technologies, (2024) SCC OnLine SC 223,
ii) Rajiv Ramanlal Shah vs. Senior Inspector of Police, Criminal Writ Petition No.1224 of 2001 dtd.
24/01/2002,
iii) S. W. Palnitkar vs. State of Bihar, (2002) 1 SCC 241,
iv) Dr. Lakhsman vs. State of Karnataka, (2019) 9 SCC 677,
v) Manohar Bhimraoji Mahalle vs. State of Maharashtra, 2020 SCC Online Bom. 368,
vi) Ajay vs. State of Maharashtra, Criminal Writ Petition No.108 of 2021 dated 21/10/2022 6.1)
Learned APP submitted that, considering the facts and circumstances of the case necessary Order may be passed.
7) Mr. Rajiv Chavan, learned Senior Advocate for Respondent Nos.2 to 6 submitted that, even though the Complainants alleged that, after the expiry of two years period they cancelled the MoU and requested for the compensation/interest amount, no notice to that effect was issued by the Complainants to the accused persons.

sentences.text: Considering these facts and the delay in filing the Application, the learned Additional Judge has rightly held that, this is purely a case of civil nature.
Hence, the rejection of the Application cannot be questioned by way of this Appeal.
8) We have given our anxious consideration to the rival submissions and perused the record carefully.

Considering the record and the rival submissions, it is evident that, even tough the Complainants alleged that they had cancelled the MoU, a prompt notice to that effect was not issued by them to the accused.

Similarly, despite the cheques of considerable amount were dishonoured,
the Complainants have not issued the statutory demand notice to accused persons.

From the MoU,
it is evident that, the prospective returns were highly excessive.
In the said Application itself the Complainants have stated that, the representations made by the accused persons were malicious.
Thus, since inception the Complainants knew the aforesaid facts, yet they entered into transaction in question and the MoU.
Therefore, it cannot be said that, the accused persons deceived the Complainants and dishonestly induced them to enter into the said MoU.

On the contrary, from a careful reading of the MoU it seems that, the Complainants entered into the said transaction on their own, willingly and after understanding its minute details only to earn an exorbitant interest knowingly taking risk of their own money.
Therefore, the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Pune has rightly held that, this is a civil P.H. Jayani 72 APEAL489.2023 FINAL.doc dispute.

9) Even though the investments in the alleged schemes were of different period, all the transactions have been clubbed together to show that, the cause of action for the same is common and just to create a picture of fraud of huge amount.

Thus, the said Application under Section 156(3) of Cr.P.C.
was nothing but a result of an improper legal advice.

10) In so far as the reported cases cited by the learned Advocate for the Complainants is concerned,
the facts of the said cases and the case in hand are distinct and therefore those are of no help to him.
10.1) In view thereof, we find no illegality in the impugned Order.
As a result, the Appeal is liable to be dismissed and is accordingly dismissed.
(SHYAM C. CHANDAK, J.)
